hypotheses: Training support changes the formation or amplification of query endpoint contrasts across encoder stages.

Another alternative is that endpoint contrasts remain large but are poorly aligned with candidate distinctions at the scorer.

hypotheses: The D01 block-0 CLS suppression could be inherited from collapsed learned input symbol embeddings for source identity pairs.

hypotheses: A support-dependent first attention write could arise predominantly from changed value vectors, attention weights, or their interaction.

diagnostics.analysis_scope: Exact block-0 CLS attention recomputation for archived I branches, with equality checks against archived post-block state; per-model summaries, discovery only.

hypotheses: Model-level averages of exact block-0 terms can reveal whether the support gap is dominated by value geometry, attention-weight routing, or cancellations.

hypotheses: A/B model-level hole versus opposite-clique comparisons can localize which exact transform contributes most to the gain gap.

Unsupported identity pairs with identical observed-neighbor sets (false twins) may be the true low-sensitivity class, while unsupported pairs with a distinguishing third identity may retain useful separation.

diagnostics.analysis_scope: Graph classes fixed by training-support specification; category summaries use models, with pair rows descriptive; discovery only.
